job.title: Automation Technician
job.description:
Industrial Automation Technologist / Technician

Location: Wetherill Park, Sydney
Industry: Advanced Manufacturing (Injection Moulding & Automation) Employment Type: Full-time, 24/7 manufacturing environment

About the Role
Our client, an established manufacturing operation based in Wetherill Park, is seeking an experienced Industrial Automation Technologist/Technician to join their team. This is a hands-on, technically diverse role supporting PLC-driven automation, industrial robotics, injection moulding machinery, and high-speed production equipment across a 24/7 site.

You'll be a key technical point of contact for production issues relating to equipment performance, product quality, and efficiency — working closely with Production, Maintenance, and Quality teams to minimise downtime and maximise OEE.
This role blends fault-finding, preventative maintenance, die setting, process optimisation, and continuous improvement, with genuine exposure to automation upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects.

Key Responsibilities
Automation & Technical Maintenance
  • Troubleshoot and maintain industrial automation and production equipment across a 24/7 environment
  • Service, repair, and set up injection moulding machines, industrial robots, IML systems, and auxiliary equipment
  • Fault-find and replace mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic components
  • Integrate industrial robots into material handling, inspection, and packaging applications, including safety interlock verification
  • Perform preventative and predictive maintenance, equipment upgrades, and calibrations
  • Complete major equipment overhauls and support complex machine, processing, and die-setting issues
Production & Process Support
  • Act as a key technical contact for production issues affecting output, quality, reliability, and efficiency
  • Perform die, insert, and colour changes, including machine start-ups and shutdowns
  • Set, adjust, and optimise robotics, machine software, and production process parameters
  • Troubleshoot production faults, including IML and high-speed packaging equipment
  • Maintain target cycle times while ensuring finished products meet specification
Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving
  • Investigate recurring and new faults using structured root-cause analysis; implement corrective and preventative actions
  • Analyse downtime, rejects, defects, and waste to identify improvement opportunities
  • Support automation design, programming, commissioning, and equipment upgrades
  • Maintain accurate records of downtime, rejects, NCRs, maintenance activities, and corrective actions
Quality & Compliance
  • Work closely with Quality Assurance to ensure equipment and processes meet product, customer, and regulatory requirements
  • Ensure compliance with site quality systems, HACCP, and applicable food safety requirements
  • Verify new or modified automation systems before production handover
Safety & Team Support
  • Work in line with WHS legislation, site safety procedures, and permit requirements
  • Identify, report, and rectify hazards and near misses
  • Coordinate with third-party service technicians when required
  • Support training and technical upskilling of production and maintenance personnel
  • Communicate and escalate technical issues across shifts to maintain operational continuity
About You
  • Proven experience in industrial automation, robotics, and/or injection moulding within a manufacturing environment
  • Strong mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic fault-finding skills
  • Experience with PLC-driven systems and industrial robot integration
  • Die-setting experience highly regarded
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, 24/7 production environment
  • Strong root-cause analysis and continuous improvement mindset
  • Food safety/HACCP exposure an advantage
  • Ability to train and support colleagues, and communicate effectively across shifts
Why Apply
  • Stable, full-time opportunity with genuine exposure to modern automation technology
  • Hands-on role combining automation, robotics, and process engineering — not a narrow, single-skill position
  • Real input into equipment upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects
  • Work within an established, well-resourced manufacturing operation

job.description:
Design & Build are partnering with a leading Australian residential building organisation to recruit a BIM / Archicad Trainer to join their People Development function.

Based in the Hunter Region, this role will support drafting teams nationally and will involve regular travel, both interstate and nationally.

Importantly, you don't need to already be an experienced trainer.

We're equally interested in hearing from experienced Archicad 29 users, Senior Drafters, BIM specialists or technical drafting professionals who enjoy helping others and would like to pivot their career into training and development.

For the right technical person, the business is prepared to invest in your development and support you in completing your Certificate IV in Training & Assessment.

The Role
Working closely with the BIM Manager and Learning & Development team, you'll become a key technical resource supporting drafting teams across the organisation.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Delivering Archicad and BIM training to drafting teams across Australia
  • Supporting the onboarding and technical induction of new starters
  • Developing structured Archicad training programs
  • Creating training materials including guides, videos, e-learning content, job aids and SOPs
  • Running face-to-face and virtual training sessions
  • Working one-on-one and with small groups to improve technical capability
  • Identifying knowledge gaps and opportunities to improve BIM processes and training
  • Working with internal technical specialists and external BIM providers
  • Monitoring training participation and effectiveness
  • Travelling nationally to support teams across different locations
About You
There are two backgrounds we're particularly interested in:

Experienced Trainer: You may already be delivering BIM, Archicad, CAD or technical training and be looking for an opportunity within a large national organisation.

Experienced Archicad User Ready for a Career Pivot: You may be a Senior Drafter, BIM Coordinator, Archicad specialist or highly experienced residential drafting professional who loves helping others and wants to move away from day-to-day drafting into a training-focused career.
Ideally, you'll bring:
  • Strong Archicad experience – Archicad 29 highly regarded
  • A background in drafting, BIM or residential construction
  • Confidence communicating technical information in a simple way
  • Strong interpersonal and presentation skills
  • An interest in coaching, mentoring and developing others
  • The ability and willingness to travel nationally
  • A proactive approach to technology and continuous improvement
  • A current driver's licence
A Certificate IV in Training & Assessment is advantageous but not essential – support can be provided to obtain this qualification for the right candidate.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is a unique opportunity to take your technical Archicad knowledge and turn it into a long-term career in training and capability development.
You'll join a major Australian building organisation, work closely with BIM and L&D specialists, gain exposure to drafting teams nationally and have the opportunity to become a recognised technical training specialist within the business.
If you're an Archicad expert who's always the person others come to for help, this could be the career pivot you've been looking for.

Apply now or contact Renee Hamilton at Design & Build Recruitment for a confidential conversation.

job.title: State Manager
job.description:
Design & Build is looking for a proven recruitment leader to take ownership of our WA business and lead its next stage of growth.

This is not a turnaround role.

You will inherit a healthy six-person team, an established client base, a recognised national brand and a Perth business that has grown year on year since launching in 2021.

The opportunity is to build on that foundation and establish one of WA’s leading specialist recruitment businesses.

The opportunity

This is a billing State Manager position, combining leadership of the WA team with continued ownership of a specialist recruitment market.

Energy & Resources is a significant growth opportunity for the business, but we are open to shaping the desk around the experience, relationships and market knowledge of the right person.

You will lead from the front by developing clients, building your market, billing personally and helping the team perform and grow. Once the WA business reaches 12 people, your personal billing responsibilities will transition out, allowing you to focus fully on leadership, strategy and continued expansion.

You will report directly to Andrew McGregor, Managing Director, with the autonomy and support to shape the future of the WA business.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading, coaching and developing the existing WA team
  • Building a high-performing specialist recruitment market
  • Growing relationships with clients across WA
  • Attracting experienced recruiters into the business
  • Setting clear standards around activity, performance and accountability
  • Identifying new markets and growth opportunities
  • Protecting and strengthening the culture as the team scales
  • Taking ownership of the WA strategy and P&L
Who we are looking for

Energy & Resources recruitment experience would be highly regarded, but it is not essential.

More important is a strong understanding of the WA market, a proven ability to build lasting client relationships and established credibility within a specialist recruitment sector.

We are open to leaders from Energy, Resources, Construction, Engineering, Infrastructure, Property or other related technical markets.

You may already be operating at State Manager level, or you may be a successful Team Leader or Manager who is ready to take the next step.

You will bring:
  • A strong background in specialist recruitment within the WA market
  • At least one to two years’ experience leading a small team
  • A proven personal billing track record
  • The ability to win work and build lasting client relationships
  • A genuine interest in developing people and growing a business
  • A leadership style aligned with our values of Honest Communication, Focus, Feedback and Care
Why Design & Build?

Design & Build has been operating for more than 20 years, with offices in Perth, Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane.

Our vision is to become Australia’s most trusted recruitment agency. We measure ourselves against a simple mission: doing right by our clients, candidates, colleagues and community.

You will also receive:
  • A 35-hour working week with flexibility around start and finish times
  • Two work-from-home days each week
  • A fully paid Christmas shutdown in addition to annual leave
  • An additional day of leave for every year of service, providing up to 30 days of annual leave after five years
  • An annual all-expenses-paid High Achievers trip
  • Structured leadership development and ongoing coaching
  • Free and unlimited access to Sonder’s 24/7 wellbeing and safety support
  • Enhanced parental and compassionate leave
  • Support from experienced national leaders across operations, finance, people and culture, learning and development, and marketing
This is a genuine opportunity to inherit a strong platform, lead an established team and build a substantial WA recruitment business.

If you are an experienced recruitment leader ready to take ownership of a state and shape its next stage of growth, we would like to hear from you.

Apply confidentially or contact Andrew McGregor for a direct conversation.

job.description:

This is a unique opportunity for someone with a strong background in quality systems and architecture/design who enjoys working collaboratively with technical teams and influencing how quality is embedded into everyday project delivery.

The Role You’ll be responsible for maintaining and continuously improving the organisation’s Quality Management System, ensuring ongoing ISO 9001 compliance while working closely with teams across the business.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Maintaining and improving the ISO 9001 Quality Management System and ensuring ongoing compliance.
  • Developing and maintaining practice standards, processes, templates and quality documentation.
  • Improving the quality, consistency and coordination of project documentation.
  • Reviewing and analysing client feedback to identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement.
  • Driving continuous improvement initiatives across the business.
  • Working closely with project and technical teams to embed quality into everyday processes.
  • Supporting teams with quality requirements, systems and best practice.
  • Providing guidance and training to help build a shared responsibility for quality across the practice.
  • Identifying opportunities to use technology and innovation to improve quality processes and outcomes.
What We're Looking For We’re looking for someone who brings:
  • Strong knowledge and practical experience with ISO 9001 and Quality Management Systems.
  • Previous experience within architecture and/or design is essential.
  • A background in a technical, quality or project delivery environment.
  • Strong understanding of documentation standards, coordination and project delivery processes.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to influence and engage stakeholders at all levels.
  • Strong organisation and attention to detail.
  • The ability to train, guide and support technical teams.
  • A proactive approach to continuous improvement and risk reduction.
  • An interest in using technology and innovation to improve quality systems.
Why Consider It?
  • Join an award-winning, design-led practice with a strong national reputation.
  • Take genuine ownership of the organisation's quality systems and continuous improvement strategy.
  • Work across a diverse range of major projects and technical teams.
  • A role with strong visibility and the opportunity to influence how quality is delivered across the business.
  • Flexible working options and a genuine focus on wellbeing and work-life balance.
  • Access to mentoring, professional development and clear career progression.
  • Be part of a collaborative environment where quality, creativity and new ideas are encouraged.
If you're a quality or technical leader with an architecture/design background and you're looking for a role where you can have a genuine impact on systems, processes and project delivery, I'd love to hear from you.

For any questions relating to this role or any other opportunities with D&B and our clients, please contact Madison Smith on 02 9376 8200 or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential

job.title: HR & Industrial Relations Professionals | Multiple FIFO Opportunities
job.description:
HR & Industrial Relations Professionals | Multiple FIFO Opportunities
Officer | Advisor | Senior Advisor

Ready to take your HR or Industrial Relations career to the next level?

We're partnering with a leading organisation delivering one of Australia's most iconic and complex infrastructure projects and are seeking multiple HR and Industrial Relations professionals across Officer, Advisor and Senior Advisor level.

These FIFO positions offer the rare opportunity to work on a nationally significant project, partnering closely with operational leaders and a diverse workforce while gaining exposure to complex people, employee relations and industrial relations matters in a fast-paced construction environment.
Whether your expertise is in Human Resources, Industrial Relations or a combination of both, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Roles Working within an experienced People & Culture team, you'll provide practical HR and / OR IR support across a major project. Depending on your experience, your responsibilities may include:
  • Providing HR and/or IR advice to managers and employees across a large blue and white-collar workforce.
  • Interpreting and applying employment legislation, Awards and Enterprise Agreements.
  • Supporting employee relations matters including performance management, misconduct, disciplinary processes and workplace investigations.
  • Managing industrial relations matters, workplace compliance and stakeholder engagement.
  • Preparing employment contracts, correspondence and HR documentation.
  • Supporting workforce mobilisation, onboarding and HR administration activities.
  • Partnering with leaders to deliver practical people solutions and coaching.
  • Assisting with HR initiatives, culture programs and continuous improvement projects.
  • Delivering HR and IR training to leaders and employees.
  • Building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders to support successful project outcomes.
About You To be successful, you'll bring:
  • Experience in Human Resources, Industrial Relations or Employee Relations.
  • Sound knowledge of Australian employment legislation, including the Fair Work Act.
  • Experience interpreting Awards and Enterprise Agreements (highly regarded).
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • A proactive, collaborative and solutions-focused approach.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Human Resources, Employment Relations, Business, Law or a related discipline will be highly regarded.
Experience within construction, infrastructure, mining, engineering or other project-based environments will be highly regarded but is not essential.
What's on Offer
  • FIFO roster with accommodation, meals and travel provided.
  • The opportunity to contribute to one of Australia's landmark infrastructure projects.
  • Multiple opportunities available across Officer, Advisor and Senior Advisor level.
  • Exposure to complex HR and Industrial Relations matters within a large-scale project environment.
  • Work alongside experienced HR and IR professionals in a collaborative and supportive team.
  • Excellent career development and progression opportunities.
  • Competitive salary packages aligned with experience.
If you're looking for a career-defining opportunity where you can make a genuine impact on a nationally significant project, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now or contact Renee Hamilton at Design & Build Recruitment for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Foreman
job.description:
Working Foreman – Luxury Residential Construction Eastern Suburbs | Projects up to $3M | $125K+ Super
We are looking for an experienced Working Foreman to join our team and take a hands-on leadership role across a range of high-end residential projects in Sydney’s Eastern Suburbs.
Our projects are valued up to $3 million, with a strong focus on quality, attention to detail and delivering luxury residential builds to a high standard.
The Role As Working Foreman, you will be responsible for the day-to-day running of your projects, coordinating trades and ensuring works are completed safely, efficiently and to program.
You will be working hands-on where required while leading a team of subcontractors and carpenters on site.
Key Responsibilities
  • Manage the day-to-day operations of residential construction sites
  • Lead and coordinate subcontractors, carpenters and trades
  • Maintain high standards of workmanship and attention to detail
  • Coordinate trades and ensure projects remain on schedule
  • Read and interpret plans, specifications and construction documentation
  • Manage site materials, deliveries and logistics
  • Maintain a clean, safe and well-organised site
  • Liaise with project managers, clients, architects and consultants
  • Identify and resolve issues quickly and effectively
  • Assist with programming and planning upcoming works
About You We are looking for someone who:
  • Has solid experience as a Foreman or Working Foreman
  • Has proven experience delivering luxury/high-end residential projects
  • Has experience working on projects valued up to $3M
  • Can confidently run and coordinate a team of subcontractors and carpenters
  • Has strong knowledge of residential construction from start to finish
  • Takes pride in quality workmanship and presentation
  • Is organised, reliable and proactive
  • Can communicate effectively with trades, management and clients
  • Has a strong understanding of site safety and construction requirements
  • Is comfortable being hands-on and leading from the front
What’s On Offer
  • Salary up to $125,000 + Super, depending on experience
  • High-end residential projects throughout Sydney’s Eastern Suburbs
  • Stable pipeline of quality projects
  • Supportive and professional team environment
  • Opportunity to take ownership of projects and progress within the business
If you're an experienced residential Foreman who takes pride in delivering high-quality luxury homes and can confidently lead a site team, we'd like to hear from you. Email Tara on trogers@designandbuild.com.au

job.title: National Government Account Manager | Workplace Solutions
job.description:
Strategic Federal Government Accounts | National Role | Workplace Solutions

The Company
Our client is a long-established Australian organisation with a strong national presence, delivering high-quality workplace products and solutions to major organisations across Australia.

Due to continued growth, they are seeking an experienced National Account Manager – Federal Government to take ownership of strategic government relationships and drive long-term growth across the sector.

The Opportunity
This is a senior, strategic relationship role focused on building and growing relationships across Federal Government.

Rather than transactional or project-by-project sales, you’ll take a longer-term approach – understanding clients' national property and workplace portfolios, developing multi-year account strategies and identifying opportunities well before they formally come to market.

You’ll work with senior stakeholders across Property, Workplace, Facilities, Procurement, Design, People & Culture and Executive teams, while partnering with internal state-based teams to deliver a coordinated national approach.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Own and develop strategic relationships across key Federal Government accounts
  • Develop 1–3-year account and growth strategies
  • Protect and grow existing relationships while identifying new Federal Government opportunities
  • Build relationships with senior government decision-makers and influencers
  • Understand clients' national workplace and property strategies to identify future opportunities
  • Grow share of wallet across existing accounts
  • Develop and negotiate national agreements, rates and preferred supplier arrangements
  • Identify opportunities to introduce additional workplace products and solutions
  • Work closely with state sales teams to deliver a consistent national client experience
  • Maintain visibility of pipeline, account activity and future opportunities
  • Support major tenders and national procurement opportunities.
About You
This role requires someone who already knows the Federal Government market. You will bring established relationships and understand how to navigate complex government stakeholder and procurement environments.
Ideally, you will have:
  • An existing network/black book of Federal Government contacts
  • 5+ years' relevant sales, business development or account management experience at Federal Government level
  • Experience managing large, complex and strategic accounts
  • Strong relationships across government Property, Workplace, Facilities and/or Procurement functions
  • A track record of both growing existing accounts and developing new relationships
  • Experience developing long-term account strategies rather than simply pursuing individual projects
  • Strong commercial and stakeholder management capability
  • Confidence engaging with senior decision-makers
  • A strategic, relationship-led approach to business development
Previous experience introducing new products or solutions to market will also be highly regarded.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an established Federal Government account professional to take ownership of a significant national portfolio and build long-term relationships within an established Australian organisation.

For any questions relating to this role or other opportunities with D&B and our clients please contact Renee Hamilton at rhamilton@designandbuild.com.au or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential

job.title: Site Engineer
job.description:
Are you a mechanically minded Site Engineer with experience across water, wastewater or infrastructure projects?

Design & Build have partnered with a leading specialist in water and wastewater solutions to find an experienced Site Engineer for a contract opportunity in Brisbane.

Location: Brisbane, QLD
Type: Contract
Duration: Initial contract with potential for further work
Rate: Negotiable based on experience

About the Role:

As Site Engineer, you’ll support the delivery of water and wastewater infrastructure projects, working closely with the Project Manager, site team, subcontractors and design consultants.

The role will have a strong focus on site coordination, technical support, QA, documentation and ensuring works are delivered safely and to program.

Projects can include pump stations, odour control systems, water treatment assets and associated infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide engineering support across live construction projects
  • Review engineering and construction drawings for buildability
  • Coordinate subcontractors, suppliers and site activities
  • Assist with procurement and tracking of materials and equipment
  • Manage QA documentation including ITPs, ITCs and inspections
  • Raise and manage RFIs and technical queries
  • Assist with project programming, cost tracking and reporting
  • Monitor construction progress and ensure works are delivered to specification
  • Liaise with design teams, consultants, suppliers and project stakeholders
  • Provide hands-on engineering support during construction and commissioning
  • Ensure compliance with quality, safety and environmental requirements
About You
  • Degree in Mechanical, Civil or Environmental Engineering, or related discipline
  • 2+ years’ Site/Project Engineering experience
  • Experience within water, wastewater, civil or infrastructure projects highly regarded
  • Strong understanding of engineering and construction drawings
  • Experience with QA, ITPs, RFIs and site documentation
  • Confident coordinating subcontractors and working with site teams
  • Mechanically minded with strong problem-solving skills
  • Able to work across multiple work fronts and hit the ground running
  • Experience with 3D modelling software such as Inventor or SolidWorks highly advantageous
What’s on Offer
  • Contract opportunity with a specialist water infrastructure business
  • Brisbane-based projects
  • Exposure to a range of water and wastewater infrastructure projects
  • Hands-on site-based engineering experience
  • Potential for ongoing contract opportunities
If you’re a Site Engineer looking for your next contract opportunity and have experience across water, wastewater or infrastructure, get in touch.

job.description:

Working closely with architects, engineers, consultants and project teams, you’ll help coordinate multidisciplinary models, maintain BIM standards and ensure high-quality project information and deliverables.

  • Lead BIM coordination across complex Aviation, Infrastructure and Data Centre projects.

Location: Sydney

Join a leading Australian EPC contractor with a strong in-house engineering team delivering major HV substation, transmission and renewable energy projects.

This is a specialist Power Systems role focused on the core studies and reports that underpin the detailed design of HV substations.

Rather than studying how different scenarios impact the wider network, you’ll be working directly alongside Primary, Secondary & Protection and LV Engineering teams, with your studies feeding into the design, equipment selection and delivery of their projects.

Why this role?
  • National offices in Sydney, Melbourne & Adelaide 
  • Genuine specialist in-house EPC engineering team
  • Major pipeline across substations, transmission, BESS and renewable energy nationally 
  • Work across the full project lifecycle from detailed design through to construction and commissioning
  • Opportunity to help grow inhouse Power Systems capability
What you’ll be doing
  • Deliver the core power systems studies that underpin HV substation design
  • Perform load flow and short circuit studies
  • Complete insulation coordination and TRV studies
  • Perform arc flash, harmonic and power quality assessments
  • Assess transformer loading and system balancing
  • Develop detailed power system models using DIgSILENT PowerFactory
  • Interpret study results and provide recommendations that directly inform substation design and equipment selection
  • Prepare technical reports, calculations and study findings
  • Provide engineering support through design, construction and commissioning
What we’re looking for
  • 5+ years’ electrical engineering experience
  • Strong Power Systems studies experience supporting detailed HV substation design
  • Hands-on DIgSILENT PowerFactory experience
  • Strong understanding of how power system studies influence substation design and equipment selection
  • Degree qualified in Electrical Engineering
  • Engineers Australia membership or eligibility
  • CPEng or working towards is highly regarded
  • Strong understanding of Australian power utility standards and requirements
Apply now or contact Jasmine on 0405 437 667 for a confidential discussion.

You will prepare take-offs, budgets and estimates, manage supplier and trade pricing, identify cost-saving opportunities and lead and mentor the estimating team.

Reporting directly to the Managing Director, you will work closely with the construction, operations and product development teams to ensure projects are accurately priced, cost-effective and aligned with the company's objectives.
This is a key role for someone who is committed, reliable and enthusiastic, with a strong focus on accuracy, efficiency, profitability and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities
  • Operate and maintain the integrated Databuild system, including cost codes, catalogues and pricing databases.
  • Maintain the flow of data between Databuild and Onsite Companion.
  • Prepare and review accurate quantity take-offs, bills of quantities and Job Analysis Reports.
  • Conduct technical plan reviews at both Preliminary Plans and Working Drawings stages.
  • Prepare detailed cost estimates for customer proposals, factoring in general and special conditions.
  • Ensure sales estimates meet required budgets and deadlines.
  • Develop scopes of works for external stakeholders.
  • Review supplier and subcontractor quotations and negotiate pricing to identify cost-saving opportunities.
  • Prepare project budgets for management approval and monitor actual costs against budget.
  • Report on project progress, costs and profitability to management.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Ensure subcontractor licences and insurances are current and accurately recorded in Onsite Companion.
  • Lead, mentor and support the estimating team.
  • Assist with internal projects and business initiatives as required.
About You To be successful in this role, you will have:
  • 5+ years' experience in construction estimating, ideally within residential building.
  • Strong, hands-on experience with Databuild, including operation, administration and maintaining pricing databases and cost codes.
  • Strong knowledge of cost estimation, bills of quantities and material take-offs.
  • Experience conducting technical plan reviews at Preliminary Plans and Working Drawings stages.
  • Experience preparing detailed budgets and analysing supplier and subcontractor quotations.
  • Strong understanding of subcontractor compliance, including licensing and insurance requirements.
  • Excellent negotiation and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • A highly analytical, organised and detail-oriented approach.
  • The ability to identify cost savings without compromising quality.
  • A proactive and results-driven approach, with a focus on process improvement.
  • The ability to manage multiple projects and changing priorities.
  • Relevant qualifications in construction management, quantity surveying or estimating, or equivalent industry experience.
Our Systems Hands-on Databuild experience is essential. The successful candidate will be trained on the other systems where required.
  • Databuild – Construction estimating, job costing and accounting.
  • Onsite Companion – Site and project management, linked with Databuild.
  • Therefore – Document management and invoice approval workflow.
The Opportunity This is an opportunity to step into a key position within a growing residential building business and have genuine ownership over the estimating function.

You will have the opportunity to lead an established estimating team, work directly with the Managing Director and contribute to improving systems, processes and profitability across the business.

If you are an experienced residential estimator with strong Databuild experience and are ready to take the next step into an Estimating Manager position, we would love to hear from you.

What We're Looking For We're looking for a practical, technically capable maintenance professional with strong fault-finding skills and experience working within a manufacturing environment.

  • Strong communication, organisation and problem-solving skills

  • Pharmaceutical or other regulated manufacturing experience is highly regarded

Why Consider the Opportunity? This is an excellent opportunity for a Maintenance Engineer looking to take on a broad, hands-on engineering position within a regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environment.
You'll have exposure to production equipment, critical utilities, reliability improvement, compliance, validation and engineering projects, making this a role with genuine technical variety.
